newsitem.title: USA: Whirlpool Q1 EPS rise on track with plan.
newsitem.headline: Whirlpool Q1 EPS rise on track with plan.

text.p: Whirlpool Corp, which reported a rise in first quarter earnings to $0.62 a share from $0.50 a year ago, said results were consistent with its plan for solid growth in 1997 operating earnings.

"Overall, we're pleased with the quarter and with the progress it represents toward our full-year goals," David Whitwam, chairman, said in a statement. "Our North and Latin American businesses again put up outstanding numbers, and European and Asian results were in line with our interim expectations for what will be meaningful operating improvement through this year."

Whirlpool said its product shipments in North America were down slightly, but less than an industry decline of two percent. However, a combination of product mix, manufacturing efficiencies and more favorable material costs boosted Whirlpool's margins in the period, it added.

Whirlpool said North America full-year 1997 industry volumes are expected to be down slightly from record levels in 1996, primarily because retail inventories of air conditioners remain high from last season.

Whirlpool Europe showed year-over-year improvement in the first quarter and increased its margins because of better product mix and gains in manufacturing efficiency, the company said. Company shipments and revenues, in local currency, were higher, despite a decline in industry volumes.
Industry shipments in Western Europe fell by about two percent in the quarter, Whirlpool said, adding full-year totals should be comparable to those for 1996.

Whirlpool recently introduced its next-generation European microwave ovens, new Bauknecht and Whirlpool brand freezers and refrigerators, and a new line of cooktops. Those and other appliance models redesigned since 1995 will account for virtually all its revenues from the region this year.

In Latin America, robust equity earnings from Brazilian affiliates drove a 16-percent jump in total regional earnings for the quarter, Whirlpool said. Outside Brazil, Latin American revenues were up slightly in the period.
Whirlpool Asia sustained a first-quarter operating loss but recorded higher year-over-year product shipments and sales.
Whirlpool Corporation makes and markets major home appliances.
